canonical_objects: a subject number constructed by the connective rather than by any noun
and-versus-or choice of were/was across two singular nouns
agreement read as the ANSWER where the connective is the CUE
decision_changed: If a site carries this, the corpus gains a case where the causal variable is built by composition rather than copied from a token, which is a stronger claim about the residual stream than any existing screen supports. A selective site licenses the standard rank-1 DAS follow-up at resid:18, and a transfer test against subject_verb_number_agreement: whether constructed number and lexical number share a direction. Registered in advance for that follow-up: >= 0.50 shared number direction, <= 0.20 distinct, between INCONCLUSIVE. If the screen returns a one-sided capability failure the registered stop rule is ONE repair of the weak side, per ops/README.md.
matched_prior_claims: circuits/task_subject_verb_number_agreement.json is a canonical behaviour, but it varies the NUMBER OF THE HEAD NOUN; here every noun is singular in every row and the subject's number is constructed entirely by the connective.

correlative_pair.both_vs_neither and its siblings put the connective on the ANSWER side -- the model predicts ' and' / ' or'. Here the connective is the CUE and agreement is the answer, so the inference runs in the opposite direction.
novelty_delta: Thirty-first behaviour. The variable is a subject number that no individual noun carries: both coordinated nouns are singular in every row, and only 'and' versus 'or' decides between ' were' and ' was'. That makes it different in kind from subject_verb_number_agreement, where a noun's own morphology carries the number and a site could in principle read it locally. Here there is no local cue to read at the prediction site -- the second noun is singular either way -- so a site that transfers this is carrying a CONSTRUCTED feature across the second noun phrase. It is also the inverse inference of the correlative screens, which predict the connective rather than reading it.
